Lessons.Title: Compare Multi-digit Numbers
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will compare two multi-digit whole numbers within 1,000,000 by reasoning about place value and to explain how you make comparisons.
Previously, you learned to build, read, name, and write multi-digit whole numbers up to six digits. You also developed an understanding of the relationship between a digit in one place and the same digit in the place immediately to its right. Through that work, you built your intuition for the relative size of numbers.
Core relationship: Multi-digit comparisons by most significant place. Compare number of digits, then compare same-position digits starting from the greatest place.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Which One Doesn’t Belong: Friendly Numbers 	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Which is Greater?	 (15 minutes); Activity 2:  Incomplete Numbers	 (10 minutes); Activity 3:  Is It Possible?	 [OPTIONAL] (20 minutes); Cool-down:  Two Numbers To Compare	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: Which is larger, 817 or 762, and by how much?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): Compare 504,210 and 540,120 using < or >.
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Comparing digits in ones place before hundreds or thousands.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Compare number of digits, then compare same-position digits starting from the greatest place.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Comparing 507,040 and 570,004 using the final digits.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The stated place value, scale, or arithmetic relationship is not preserved.
CommonMistakes.Correction: The ten-thousands places determine the result.
